reason: The text explicitly establishes and reinforces strict hierarchical structures throughout. Joseph's narrative demonstrates clear master-servant relationships (Potiphar and Joseph, the prison captain and Joseph), authority over household servants and prisoners, and respectful deference to those in positions of power. Joseph's success and favor (וַיִּמְצָא יוֹסֵף חֵן בְּעֵינָיו) come precisely through his faithful operation within these hierarchical systems, not through challenging them. The text repeatedly emphasizes titles, authority structures, and Joseph's subordinate positions (עֶבֶד, serving פַּרְעֹה's officials). Nothing in the passage suggests hierarchy is unimportant or discouraged; rather, it is foundational to the narrative structure.
